title: Band-9 Samples: When do people give gifts or presents in your country?
passage_text: This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 9 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 1 Test 2 question: “When do people give gifts or presents in your country?” Sample 1 Female Male In my country, gift-giving is a common tradition on birthdays. It’s an expression of love and appreciation towards the person celebrating their annual milestone. Friends and family usually give presents that align with the recipient’s interests or needs. Sample 2 Female Male In the professional sphere, it’s not uncommon to give gifts in recognition of someone’s accomplishments. It could be a promotion, completing a challenging project, or celebrating a company anniversary. These gestures foster a positive work environment. Sample 3 Female Male Gift-giving largely hinges on cultural festivals in my country. For instance, during Lunar New Year, it’s typical to exchange presents like traditional sweets or red envelopes. That said, it’s a flexible custom and varies from one region to another. Sample 4 Female Male In my country, it’s customary to bestow gifts on special occasions, like birthdays or weddings. It’s a way of expressing our affection and good wishes towards the recipient. However, the practice isn’t set in stone and really depends on personal or family traditions. Sample 5 Female Male In my country, when a baby is born, it’s customary for friends and family to bring gifts to the new parents. This could be items such as baby clothes, toys, or even supplies like diapers and baby formula. Sample 6 Female Male When a person retires, it’s a common practice to give them a gift to honor their years of service. This could be a watch, a plaque, or even a trip to a place they’ve always wanted to visit. Sample 7 Female Male Well, in my country, we don’t really have particular times for giving gifts. It’s more about random acts of kindness. You could get a gift from someone at any moment, for any reason, or no reason at all. It’s a way to keep life exciting and full of surprises. Sample 8: Not Sure Female Male Well, in the country where I reside, which I’m not exactly certain of at the moment, people are generally inclined to exchange gifts during universal celebrations. These might be occasions such as Christmas, New Year’s, and birthdays. It’s a way of expressing affection, extending warm wishes, and celebrating milestones. Sample 9: Not Sure Female Male I must admit, I’m not entirely certain about the gift-giving customs in my country. However, if I were to venture a guess, I’d say birthdays are probably a common occasion for that. Sample 10: Not Sure Female Male To tell you the truth, I don’t have a clear answer as to when we usually give gifts in my country. It’s possible that anniversaries could be one of those times, as it’s typical to commemorate such occasions with presents in many cultures.
